Subject: MAP: Data handling & compliance milestone — follow-up and responsibilities

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the call today — really appreciate the context on HealthSync's ingestion pipeline and PHI scoping. As discussed, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) section focused on Data Handling & Compliance so we can align on milestones, owners, and dependencies.

Quick recap of what we captured:
- Milestone: Define data retention & logging policy for PHI/PII flows
  - Responsible: HealthSync (policy owner) / Redwood (technical implementation)
  - Target close date: 2026-10-15
  - Dependencies: SOC 2 report access, KMS key agreement for CME (customer-managed encryption)
- Milestone: Audit trail & access logging enablement
  - Responsible: Redwood infra (enable logging) / HealthSync security (log retention policy)
  - Target close date: 2026-10-15
- Milestone: PHI scoping & acceptable data transformations
  - Responsible: HealthSync product/security (scope) / Redwood engineering (transformations/filters)
  - Target close date: 2026-10-08

Next steps I propose:
1) You and your security lead review the attached draft map and flag any gaps by EOD 9/30.
2) Dev (cc'd) will provide implementation notes (retention, logging, KMS) and a short checklist for on-prem vs hosted by 10/1.
3) We'll get SOC 2 summary evidence to you (Redwood security) as part of the dependency items — I'll share the link once Rishi reviews.

Please let me know if these owners/dates look right, or if you'd prefer alternate assignees.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Alex King <alex.king@healthsync.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthSync Security Team <security@healthsync.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Data handling & compliance milestone — follow-up and responsibilities

Marissa,

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifying questions from security:
1) PHI/PII scope: we handle both direct identifiers and limited data sets. Do you support configurable field-level redaction/transformations before data leaves HealthSync?
2) Retention: our policy is 7 years for certain records. Can Redwood configure per-route retention and automated purge, or is retention solely on our side?
3) Audit logs: we need immutable audit trails for read/write operations with 1:1 user IDs. Can you confirm what is captured (request metadata, user-id, model-id, prompt/response hashes) and retention windows?
4) KMS: does Redwood support customer-managed keys (Bring Your Own Key) in Hosted mode, or would that require Private deployment?

If Dev can answer on (1)-(4) and provide a short checklist, we can review and confirm ownerships. Also please include the SOC 2 Type II date range in the evidence.

Best,
Alex King
Head of Security Operations, HealthSync
alex.king@healthsync.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex King <alex.king@healthsync.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T08:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Data handling & compliance milestone — follow-up and responsibilities

Thanks Alex — below are concise answers and an implementation checklist. I kept it focused so you can paste into your security review.

1) Field-level redaction/transformations:
- Redwood supports request-time transformations via ingestion hooks and pipeline filters. We provide two approaches: (a) customer-side pre-processing (recommended for PHI minimization), or (b) Redwood-managed transformations (we can apply deterministic hashing or tokenization on configured fields).
- Responsibility: HealthSync to provide list of fields to redact/transform; Redwood engineering to implement filters for supported model routes.

2) Retention:
- Per-route retention: Supported on Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted, we support configurable short-term KV/prefix caching retention and a configurable message retention policy for logs/inputs up to a customer-configurable retention period (subject to plan limits).
- Automated purge: Yes — we can configure automatic purge jobs tied to retention windows.
- Responsibility: Redwood engineering to implement retention config; HealthSync to define policy and scope.

3) Audit logs (what's captured):
- Standard audit events: request timestamp, request-id, model-id, route, response status, user-id (if forwarded in headers), input/response hashes (not full content unless enabled), and associated KV/cache events.
- Immutability: Logs are write-once in our storage tier and can be exported to your SIEM (S3/Cloud Storage) for long-term immutable retention.
- Retention windows: Configurable; we can retain in-host for short-term and ship to customer storage for long-term retention.

4) KMS / Customer-managed keys (CMK):
- Hosted: We support envelope encryption and can integrate with major KMS providers for key wrapping. Full BYOK (customer-managed HSM) for hosted requires a contractual agreement and additional controls (we can do CME via partner flow).
- Private/Dedicated: Native BYOK/HSM support available.

Implementation checklist (deliverables):
- [ ] Finalize PHI field list (HealthSync) — due 2026-10-05
- [ ] Confirm retention windows per data class (HealthSync) — due 2026-10-06
- [ ] Redwood to provide config for per-route retention + purge (Engineering) — deliverable 10/01 (attached short config guide)
- [ ] SOC2 summary & evidence to be shared (Redwood Security) — Rishi to review and share by 10/02
- [ ] KMS integration plan (Redwood Ops) — draft by 10/07

I've attached a condensed config guide and SOC2 evidence summary for your security team. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min tech deep-dive with our infra team this week.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

Attachments: SOC2_AuditEvidence_summary.pdf, SOC2-AuditEvidence.zip

Marissa
